a40693b7e8c38d035d60b1444515c83dc2020ffe: A resort on a human scale, Les Bugnenets-Savagnières focuses on the quality of its welcome and its closeness rather than on impressive figures. Its 30 km of runs are a good fit for a 3 to 4 day stay, especially with families or for skiers who don't need to constantly change their playground. Les Bugnenets-Savagnières has earned its family reputation: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Jura for getting children started on skiing. The moderate altitude of Les Bugnenets-Savagnières, starting at 1078 m and rising to 1449 m, makes it sensitive to changes in the weather. January and February remain the safest months for optimal snow cover. Outside that window, checking the snow reports before you set off is strongly advised. At €46 for a day lift pass, Les Bugnenets-Savagnières sits in the mid-range for budget among resorts: neither cheap nor exorbitant. The quality of the ski area and its facilities justifies this price for most skiers. In short, Les Bugnenets-Savagnières doesn't compete with the ski giants and doesn't pretend to. It is an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.

a43e54d6af2caafbb7aaf7a36ea46b7bebb053e1: With its 155 km of runs, the Folgarida ski area offers something for every type of skier: big enough not to go round in circles for a week, yet compact enough to find your favourite sectors easily. Technical terrain reigns at Folgarida: with 22 black and 46 red runs on offer, experienced skiers will find plenty to really challenge themselves. Off-piste and freeride are enjoyed in often excellent conditions, thanks to the altitude and the aspect of the slopes. A few exceptionally mild winters can cause tight conditions early in the season, but the situation recovers quickly once the first decent snowfalls arrive. Budget-wise, a stay in Folgarida is clearly on the higher side: 85€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants among the most expensive in the Alps.
